target_claim: For every vector space V of dimension n ≤ 5 and every Zariski-closed subgroup H ⊆ GL(V) satisfying the stated irreducibility and fixed-vector hypotheses, H equals PSL(2).
source_quote:
\begin{thm} \label{thm: punt}
Let $V$ be a vector space of dimension $n \le 5$ over an
algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.
Let $H \subseteq \GL(V)$ be a  Zariski closed subgroup, and assume that the
connected component of the identity $H^0$ acts irreducibly on $V$.  Suppose that every
$h \in H$ has a fixed vector in $V$. Then
$H = \PSL(2)$, $n$ is odd, and $V \simeq \Sym^{n-1}(W)$ where
$W$ is the standard representation of $\SL(2)$.
For a generic semi-simple element $h \in H$, one has $\dim(V|h = 1) = 1$.
\end{thm}
